subject: Will World Models Eat Physical AI?
text:
Hi [NAME],

We hosted a deep-dive webinar on the future of AI in robotics, and given
your work, I thought you would have found the discussion particularly
relevant.

We brought together Chris Paxton (AI Lead at Agility) and Jason Ma
(Co-founder at Dyna) for a conversation moderated by Encord CEO [SENDER] and Head of Physical AI [SENDER] to debate a central question: "Will
World Models Eat Physical AI?"

The discussion focused on World Models vs. VLAs, real-world deployment
trade-offs, and the data pipelines powering current humanoid and robotics
systems.

Attaching the recording here
<[LINK]>
-
we hope you enjoy the session, and I'd love to hear your thoughts!

subject: VLAs - multi captioning with Encord
text:
Hi [NAME] - nice to meet you, 

I noticed that you're leading the VLA team at [COMPANY] - congratulations on the promotion and it is exciting to see the team scale! It's clear you're leaning into VLA models for real-world autonomy, which closely aligns with what we're seeing across our ADAS customers. 

Encord has helped leading teams such as Boston Dynamics and Toyota - providing a scalable platform to help teams gain greater control of their VLA training data pipelines & support frontier use cases such as egocentric manipulation captioning + human-in-the-loop preference capture.

We also recently hosted a session with folks from Agility and Dyna on VLAs and world models - sharing the recording here. 

Would you be open to a quick 20-minute chat to trade notes and for me to introduce how we're helping similar teams?

subject: Invite to AI leaders roundtable - May 21st
text:

subject: model performance feedback loop
text:
Hi [NAME],

We recently began working with Veriff and Onfido, and [COMPANY] came up given your work in the IDV space. 

One theme we're hearing a lot: once models are live, the challenge shifts to diagnosing failure modes and tightening the loop between training data and production - especially in high-staked KYC/AML settings. 

Curious if that's something you're seeing as well on your side?

Happy to compare notes if useful. I'm usually flexible Tue - Thu.

subject: ISC West [YEAR]
text:
hi [NAME],

Hope ISC West this year went well for Brivo!

We haven't met, but I saw you evaluated Encord last year so wanted to
reconnect, given your recent Eeva launch.

We're seeing a similar pattern: teams start with CVAT or internal data
management tools, but run into scaling issues with large video datasets,

with on-prem/edge deployment and agen-based auto-labeling and QA workflows.

Worth a quick connect?

subject: [SENDER] pointed me your way (perception side of Copper One)
text:
Hey [NAME],

[SENDER] forwarded your name, he thought you'd be the right person to ask.

I had a thought on the perception side of Copper One. With spot patrols,
pronto's camera stack and aerial surveys all live now, Im curious if the
team is training site specific models on top of vendor outputs vs. running
everything out-of-box. The vendors are good, but there's usually a gap when
you want anomaly detection or near-miss events tuned to your actual site.

We work with Boston Dynamics on the data infrastructure side of that exact
problem: curation, annotation, model eval. If it's a real workflow at
Mariana, I'd love to chat. If it's all vendor-handled it would also be
useful to know.
